summary: Embedding distribution variance ('entropy surge') triggers ANN fallback and 99th-percentile rerank latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-10 02:14 UTC QuillSearch reported intermittent but sharp increases in 99th-percentile latency for the /rerank endpoint on their dedicated cluster. Impact: customer-facing search UI experienced slow 'load more' responses and occasional 503s for heavy queries. Hypothesis at intake: unusual embedding distribution (high variance in vector norms / 'entropy surge') caused the ANN routing layer to consider many shards as low-confidence resulting in fallback to exact scan or CPU-based path, increasing tail latency and causing queue buildup.

Environment: Dedicated cluster for QuillSearch (dedicated-gpu-pool-7), production, primary region us-east with cross-region reads to eu-west. Ingest pipeline: embed service rwd/embed-tilt-1.1 -> indexer -> ANN index (hnsw) served by rerank-fast-v2.

Observed behaviour: 1) 99th pct latency for rerank increased from ~180ms to >4s in bursts. 2) Request traces show ANN index returning empty or low-confidence candidate sets then triggering exact-scan fallback. 3) GPU metrics show periodic KV-cache churn and increased cpu fallback tasks on indexer nodes. 4) Embedding norm distribution (per-request histograms) shows abrupt spikes in variance and a long tail of high-magnitude vectors.

Expected behaviour: Stable rerank 99th <= 300ms for this workload; ANN index should return consistent candidate sets and avoid frequent CPU fallbacks.

Customer impact: QuillSearch reports degraded UX and increased error rate during peak indexing windows. They are on a dedicated capacity contract; SLA implications active.
steps_to_reproduce: Send a burst of 5000 mixed-text queries (long-tail distribution) to customer rerank endpoint during an ongoing ingest backfill
Observe 99th-percentile latency and check /metrics/ann/fallback_count on indexer nodes
Capture embedding norm histograms from embed service by enabling debug header x-rwd-embed-debug: norms=1 for a 10-minute window
Trigger a controlled backfill with a known heavy-tail document set (provided by customer) to reproduce entropy surge

comments: 2026-03-10 02:25 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Intake from QuillSearch with sample request IDs and attached traces. Customer indicates issue began after a content backfill earlier that morning.
2026-03-10 03:05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed elevated ann.fallback_count on dedicated-gpu-pool-7 between 02:12-02:20 UTC. Correlated with indexer CPU spike and disk IO on node indexer-3.

2026-03-10 04:10 - Emma Zhang (Index Team): Observed increased L2-norm variance across embed batches; suspect transient encoder change in customer's ingest pipeline (external to Redwood) injected very long vectors. Requested sample vectors for analysis.
2026-03-10 08:30 - QuillSearch (Customer): Provided sample documents and confirmed a third-party scraper changed tokenization producing extremely long text fields during backfill.

2026-03-11 11:12 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Applied temporary routing throttles to reduce burst load to the affected index shards and increased ann.search_k parameter to avoid immediate exact-scan fallback. Observed reduction in tail latency in next 2 hours.

2026-03-12 09:45 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and proposed follow-ups: reindex with normalized embeddings, add client-side embed validation, and telemetry alert for embedding-norm variance. Customer acknowledged and accepted plan.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Embedding norm variance ('entropy surge') caused ANN heuristics to underperform—many nodes judged candidate sets below confidence threshold and triggered exact-scan fallback.

Hypothesis B: Intermittent routing skew pushed 60% of traffic to indexer-3 which had partial LRU cache coldness due to prior restarts; combined with heavy vector norms led to increased disk reads and CPU fallback.
Reproducer run: Controlled backfill reproduced norm-skew within 12 minutes and triggered ann.fallback_count > 250 in 3m window.
Metric correlation: ann.fallback_count correlates with embed.norm_stdev > 0.5 and indexer.disk_io > baseline by 4x. GPU utilization remained moderate—bottleneck was index CPU and disk path.
Checked model version headers: embed requests carried header embed_version: rwd/embed-tilt-1.1 across samples. No evidence of on-the-fly model switch inside Redwood.
workaround: Applied routing throttle on cluster-level to smooth bursts (temporary).
Increased ANN search_k and probe parameters to reduce fallback rate (config change rolled to affected shards).
Requested customer to pause their backfill and normalize texts (truncate very long fields) before re-ingest.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11): routing throttle + increased ANN probe reduced 99th pct latency from >4s to ~280-350ms during replicated burst tests.
Temporary mitigation will remain until customer completes reindex with normalized embeddings. Scheduled reindex window: 2026-03-14 01:00-03:00 UTC.

Follow-up action items:
- DEV-1348: Add embedding-norm telemetry and an alert when batch stdev exceeds threshold (assigned to Index Team).
- OPS-2291: Add adaptive fallback circuit breaker to prevent cluster-wide exact-scan storms by isolating affected shards.
- DOCS-88: Add guidance to dedicated customers about embedding size limits and recommended client-side validation.
Postmortem plan: If reindex does not normalize distribution, run deeper index tuning (hnsw param sweep) and consider a pre-filter step to cap vector norms during ingestion.
